partnershipPlan: A patient partner who waited overnight in the emergency department and a bed manager review the reference standard definition and the plain-language summary.
socialListening: No social media listening; complaints about waits for a bed over the last year are themed by time of day.

items.quote: Composite paraphrase: They told me a bed was coming at midnight; I got to the ward at nine in the morning.
items.implication: Report the flag's accuracy at night separately.

items.quote: Composite paraphrase: The screen lights up the patients we already know will wait; it is the quiet ones on the medicine list who get stuck.
items.implication: Report accuracy by admitting service and compare with occupancy alone.

items.quote: Composite paraphrase: Every flag is a phone call; half of them sort themselves out before I finish dialling.
items.implication: Count escalations triggered by false-positive flags.

items.quote: Composite paraphrase: Nobody could tell us whether it would be one hour or ten.
items.implication: Consider whether a calibrated score could support honest wait estimates for families.

summary: Four composite voices on overnight waits, missed patients, escalation workload and uncertainty for families.
